questions.question: English Idioms & Phrases #16: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: 'Hit the nail on the head'
options: To state something with exact accuracy
questions.hint: To describe exactly what is causing a situation.

questions.question: English Idioms & Phrases #17: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: 'Beat around the bush'
options: To avoid discussing the main topic directly
questions.hint: To speak evasively without coming to the point.

questions.question: English Idioms & Phrases #18: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: 'Call it a day'
options: To stop working on something for the rest of the day
questions.hint: To decide to stop working.

questions.question: English Idioms & Phrases #19: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: 'Once in a blue moon'
questions.hint: An event that happens very rarely.

questions.question: English Idioms & Phrases #20: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: 'Through thick and thin'
options: Under all circumstances, good and bad
questions.hint: Supporting someone through all difficulties.

questions.question: English Idioms & Phrases #21: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: 'To spill the beans'
questions.hint: 'Spill the beans' means to reveal secret information.

questions.question: English Idioms & Phrases #22: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: 'Bite the bullet'
options: To get injured in a fight
To face a difficult situation with courage
questions.hint: 'Bite the bullet' means to endure a painful situation bravely.

questions.question: English Idioms & Phrases #23: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: 'A blessing in disguise'
options: An apparent misfortune that yields unexpected good results
questions.hint: Something that seems bad at first but turns out good.

questions.question: English Idioms & Phrases #24: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: 'Burn the midnight oil'
options: To work or study late into the night
questions.hint: To study or work until late at night.

questions.question: English Idioms & Phrases #25: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: 'Throw in the towel'
questions.hint: To give up or accept defeat.
